verification_performed.seventh_bypass_probe_flatten_plain_text: Actively probed both directions per the task brief. (a) Bypass direction: none found -- flatten_plain_text/1 only ADDS a text_scan detection alongside the unchanged per-node structural checks (walk_node/1 still runs independently); it can never suppress an existing detection, and its own recursion is unconditional/whole-subtree so it cannot itself be evaded by nesting depth or additional sibling structure. (b) Over-rejection direction: CONFIRMED, but not a security-invariant violation. flatten_plain_text/1 recurses into every non-code/pre element's children and walk/1's list clause joins ALL siblings at a given level with NO separator -- and critically, this includes the ROOT block list itself (paragraphs, list items, etc. are ordinary elements, not excluded like code/pre), so the projection effectively concatenates the ENTIRE document's prose (minus code/pre) into one string for the raw-tag-shape scan, not just one inline formatting run. Reproduced two concrete false positives that did NOT trigger before this round's fix: (1) two adjacent paragraphs 'Configure with a<' / 'b>c or make it safe' (a stray '<' ending one paragraph, an unrelated 'b>c' starting the next) now cross-concatenates to '...a<b>c...' and is wrongly rejected as raw HTML; (2) ordinary prose using '<'/'>' as comparison operators split by emphasis, 'if a<b and *count* >d then continue', is wrongly rejected the same way. (The single-le, no-formatting case 'if a<b and c>d then continue' was ALREADY rejected before this round -- that part is pre-existing over-rejection, not new; only the cross-sibling/cross-paragraph concatenation is new this round.) This is a genuine availability/UX regression -- legitimate help-content authors using bare angle brackets as comparison operators or generic-type notation, split across any inline formatting or across paragraphs, will have valid drafts rejected -- but it is strictly one-directional (over-restrictive, never under-restrictive) and touches no tenant-isolation, secret, SQL-injection, or crash invariant. Not gating on it; flagged below for routing.
